instruction: find the {object} by turning your waist, without walking, and point at it with your right arm. The first time the measured aim shows the arm on the {object}, say "I found it!". Then keep pointing at it until you are told to stop, because it may be moved: listen about 3 seconds at a time, and after each listen find the {object} again in the new image. If it has moved, point again at where it is now (use its new place in the image; the measured aim is only how far the arm misses the place you last aimed at, so the image decides whether it moved). If it is where it was but the measured aim shows the arm off it, point again too. If you lose it, look around for it with your waist. If you cannot find it after looking around, say so and give up. When you are told to stop, lower your arm and finish with done

object.note: what to point at, as the person named it (a water bottle, the red chair, the teacher's laptop)

safety_notes: Do not walk in this task: search by turning the waist and point with the right arm only.
notes: No walking or exploring (walks: false). The waist turns (yaw: look, point_to aims by it) but never tilts: tilts_waist false holds its roll and pitch at 0 and the whole waist stiff (waist_lock_kp/kd) in every arm_sdk message; tilting the torso tipped the robot (2026-11-07). Keep pointing until told to stop (said, or typed in g1 start while it runs; Esc stops it at once): the model finds the object again in each new image after a ~3 s listen and re-points when it has moved (the image decides: the measured aim is relative to the last target) or the arm is off it. g1 start fills {object} from the request ("point at the water bottle": the model's run_task object, or /task point_at water bottle). g1 run point_at uses the default, the laptop, in point_at_the_laptop's scene (45 degrees to the right: the waist turns), scored by the twin; a voice says stop after 60 s. Budget: 300 decisions or 30 min (a guess).
